overview: This one-page list of papers catalogs three communications filed under aerial-navigation facilities and landing fields in Japanese-ruled Taiwan. The entries concern a proposed flight by Moye W. Stephens and Richard Halliburton using a military drill ground as a temporary landing field, a 1935 report on a new aviation field at Taihoku, and the 1936 inauguration of a public aviation field at Giran, with the latter two reports drawing upon notices in the Official Gazette of the Government-General of Taiwan.

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning aviation fields in Taiwan
subfiles.about: An index sheet lists three communications concerning proposed flights and the establishment of aviation fields in Japanese-ruled Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: The first entry records a May 17 communication from Amoy concerning the proposed flight of Moye W. Stephens and Richard Halliburton over Taiwan and a map supplied by the Japanese consul showing a military drill ground prepared as a temporary landing field. The second describes George W. Maney's despatch of September 27, 1935, reporting a new aviation field at Taihoku and enclosing a translation of an official notice. The third lists Maney's communication of July 15, 1936, on the inauguration of a public aviation field at Giran, enclosing Taiwan Government-General Notice No. 111 of July 14, 1936.

interest: The sheet provides a compact view of the expansion and formal regulation of civil aviation infrastructure in colonial Taiwan during the mid-1930s. It is particularly useful for linking an unusual proposed flight by the adventurer Richard Halliburton and aviator Moye W. Stephens with Japanese consular assistance and a temporary military landing ground. The references to translated Government-General notices also identify potentially valuable sources for studying the administrative development of the aviation fields at Taipei and Yilan.
